Okay. Let's head to Ushijima-san's restaurant, shall we?
Hope we can get something useful.
(Ushijima-san's place is on Kumano Boulevard.)
What you got there? Looks like something an official scorer would compile.
Oh, this data's better than your average scorer's.
Where'd you get this? Someone from the Wyverns?
Don't tell me... Have you been putting together pitching data all this time?
No matter how much I try... I just can't say goodbye to baseball.
Hold up. There's more than just Sawada on there.
This data highlights the pitchers of all twelve major clubs. Course, pitch type, speed, accuracy⑬it's all there.
Takasugi-san. Remember when I said I can't just hit a home run even if I knew what pitch was coming?
That's actually only half true.
In the pros, just swinging at whatever comes won't make you any good.
You have to go to bat knowing about eighty percent of what the pitcher's gonna throw.
How often you can turn those into hits is what separates the best from the rest.
So you're saying you deliberately went to hit that home run?
Yeah. I knew what was coming.
I knew after six straight curveballs on a 0-2 count, Sawada would go for a fastball.
Then what are you trying to prove by poring over this stuff?
Don't tell me you can somehow pinpoint the Nagoya Family through pitching data?
No, I was checking to see if what Manabe-san and Sakai-san said was true.
Which was?
Manabe-san said the match fixing stopped as soon as I was banned from the league.
This data backs it up. It's like the Wyverns completely transformed after that game.

It might not be obvious to the untrained eye, but any weird
pitch selections or random bench-shuffling altogether
vanished from their play.
You can tell that just from the data?
You might be surprised how much baseball adheres to set patterns of play.
Can't argue there.
That's not all. After my one and only game, the Wyverns completely changed their roster.
Their policy used to favor local talent, but all of a sudden they went after foreign players and actively engaged in trades.
But that's the opposite of what Sakai said. Didn't he say you were sacrificed to protect Nagoya?
What else could he mean but protecting local players?
Could be. But I think when Sakai-san mentioned Nagoya, it wasn't just about our old team.
I'm thinking it's something bigger. Like something that concerns the whole town.
All of Kineicho?
We both know this town has a dark side, but we're clueless about what happens in the shadows.
Now, if we want to find more about the Nagoya Family, we're gonna have to search beyond just baseball.
So that scandal of yours really did change the face of this town. And you're saying we get to the bottom of it.
Isn't there anyone who's in the know about these things?
There's a perfect guy for that. He's really well-known here in town.
The Chamber of Commerce chairman and esteemed local chef, Ushijima-san.
He's treated me good ever since I wound up here. Whatever kind of secret's going on around these parts, he would know.
So, what is it you wanted to ask me?
It's a question about Nagoya.

Oh? I never took you for one of those concerned citizen
types.
Well, let's just say I have to write a non-sexy article for once. That's all it is.
Look, did something abruptly change around here 15 years back?
For instance, I heard the Nagoya Family started popping up around that time.
What, so now you're after details about the Nagoya Family? Then I've got nothing to tell you.
We owe the Nagoya Family our livelihood.
15 years ago, Kineicho was a bloody nightmare.
Honjincho Street was caught in a turf war between the Tojo Clan and the Omi Alliance.
Those militants were always causing some sort of scuffle or strife. Not to mention crime.
But it's so peaceful now.
Back then, the Tojo and the Omi controlled the baseball betting business.
Plus this city's caught right between them, so any conflicts they had spilled over into our everyday lives.
But after a certain incident, the two gangs were suddenly forced out of Nagoya.

That match fixing scandal with the Wyverns 15 years ago.
You don't remember?
Oh, yeah, that.
Well, I'm not really a sports person, so I can't say I know all the details.

But the scandal brought baseball betting under the law's
watchful eye. And evidently, that was enough to push the
Tojo and the Omi out of Nagoya for good.
With those two tyrants gone, the Nagoya Family stepped in to clean up their mess.
They've been looking after our town ever since.

They're still yakuza, no doubt, but they don't start
conflicts or run protection on us.

By and large, we all get to live out our days in peace...
in exchange for one little major league hiccup.
A sacrifice for Nagoya...
The dots are starting to connect.
So, I take it you know who the boss of this Nagoya Family is?
I can't imagine why you'd want to know, but I suggest you give that up.
I couldn't tell you who's in charge, and I don't give a damn. The Nagoya Family protects us behind the scenes.
For anyone doing business in this town, that's all we need to know.
Ta-chan!? Please, I need your help! They took my brother away!
They took Toriyama-san? Who?
I don't know. One of the men had a wound on his cheek.
I'm following them now. I'm near Warehouse 62 at the port. Ahhh⑬!
Milky-chan!?
Takasugi-san, there's somewhere I need to be!
Sheesh. If you're going, I have to go too, dammit.
Okay, Ushijima-san. If you think of anything, let me know.
Oh, uh, I don't have to put this coffee on a tab, do I?
Hey, what are you doing here at this hour? Come to settle your tab?
Actually, I came here to ask you something.
I told you, you're banned until you pay me in full.
In that case, I'll cover it.
And you must be the loan shark shaking Shinada down. Haven't heard much good about you.
Don't know what kind of horror stories you're hearing, but all my clients love me.
Well, as far as I'm concerned, whoever pays the bill is a valued customer.
Huh? What the hell? You ran up a tab this high?
You're not gonna, um...?
Of course I'm tacking this on to your loan.
In this rhythm action game, you press buttons in time with a song. When the bar beneath the lyrics reaches a button icon, press that button and you're good to go.
If your timing is way off or if you press the wrong button, it'll count against you.
Well-timed, accurate button presses will score you lots of points, but too many mistakes and the song will come to an abrupt end.
Complete the game by singing (or letting your partner sing) a song from start to finish. Familiarize yourself with each song and perfect your technique as you aim for a new high score.

<Color:14>You can choose to switch between English and Japanese lyrics
in the Options Menu.<Color:Default>

Your time is almost up. Would you like to extend your session for 500 yen?

(I don't have any cash on me, so...)
　No, thanks.
Yeah, sounds good.
An extension? Yes, sir. Thank you very much. Enjoy your time.
Thank you very much. Please bring your microphones and your check to the front before leaving.

(Ain't got much money, so...)
　Nah, I'm gonna pass.
Sure, why not?

(I'm a little light on cash, so...)
　I don't think so.

(I'm short on cash, so that's it for now.)
　No, thank you.
Yes, I'd like to stay a bit longer.
An extension? Yes, miss. Thank you very much. Enjoy your time.
(You're in good hands, Uno-san. Now to find me a cab to Warehouse 62. It's at the port, so Takasugi-san shouldn't be long after.)
(Gotta catch a cab to Warehouse 62, dockside. What did Milky-chan's brother get himself into this time?)
Uno-san? What's he want now?
Sorry, Uno-san, but we're a little busy here!
Shinada, get out while you still can!
Uno-san? What's wrong!?
These bastards showed up and... Gwah!
Hey, what're you doing on the phone? We have to hurry.
It's Uno-san. He's in trouble! We have to check on him first!
...You shitting me?
Hang on! Stay with me, Uno-san!
I'll call an ambulance! Shinada, go help your friends!
I'll be right behind you. And I'd better not find your ass dead!

(That's Warehouse 62 up ahead. Milky-chan and her brother
might be inside!)
Milky-chan, are you all right!?
Milky-chan, where is he? Where'd they take your brother?
Ta-chan, I'm sorry.
Ugh... Ushijima-san?
We got orders to take you out, Shinada.
It's your fault for not heeding the warnings.
If only you'd gotten scared away from all those incidents in town... it wouldn't have come to this.
You wanted to know about the Nagoya Family so bad? Well here's your answer.
I don't believe it... I <Italic>won't</Italic> believe it.
Any last words? We've known each other all of 15 years. I can listen to your will at least.
Hah. I know you're all good people. So you can stop playing the villain any time now.
Maybe I was too dumb for school, but I did learn how to read people.
And I know that every one of you opened your hearts to me!
That's why I can't believe your little gangster act!
Those accidents around town, and Sakai-san's death⑬you're saying you're behind all that!?
You all sold out to the Nagoya Family!?
Buddy. We <Italic>are</Italic> the Nagoya Family. A group of ordinary citizens dedicated to the cause.

Now I don't like the idea of being considered yakuza, but I
guess that's how it goes.

Ushijima-san, if you really wanted to kill me, you could've
done so anytime you wanted.
But you didn't. Why is that?
Somebody's forcing you, aren't they?
And you're only doing this because you're following their orders, right?
Tell me who it is!
Milky, just do it already.
What are you asking? You're gonna make a girl do it?
I, uh... Ushijima-san?
Fine then. I'll end it.
Tatsuo, you okay now?
Uh-huh. Good to go.
Then make sure you prepare for what's ahead.
There's no telling what may happen in Tokyo.
Okay. Will do.
Huh? Dojima, you said? Wait... could it be?
Let's see... Huh, where are you?

I swear, I remember a Dojima-kun in Homeroom 1 who had the
best grades in the class. Uh...
I was in Homeroom 1 all right, but I'm not in that yearbook.
Huh? Why not?
Because I never graduated. I was expelled.
You were!?

I caused some major trouble the summer of our third year...
I ended up graduating from juvie instead.
Juvie? Huh? As in juvenile detention!?
I had it out with a gang from Kamuro Tech High.
Kamuro Tech? They were Tokyo's worst bad-boy school. We played them in the East Tokyo Final.
Huh? Wait. There was someone who fought a whole bunch of Kamuro Tech guys all by himself the day before our regional final. Was that...
I remember that. Those punks from Kamuro Tech were threatening our players to forfeit the final.
But the day before the game, they all got sent to the emergency room.
That let us play the final without interference. We won and went on to nationals!
And at Koshien, we lost 2 to 1 in the first round, to Sawada and the rest of Chukyo Academy.
Your home run was our only hit. I saw it on TV, in a waiting room at family court.

But man, that blows my mind... I had no idea you saved our
hides back then. Why would you put yourself through that?
For me, seeing the baseball team make it to nationals at Koshien...
No, for everyone at West Kamuro that summer, that was our dream.
Your dream?
Yeah. You were the one who gave us that dream in the first place.
